scheme_name: Amrita University – Ammachi Labs Social Innovation Fund
overview: Amrita University – Ammachi Labs Social Innovation Fund is a research initiative focused on social innovation, women's empowerment, and community development through technology-driven solutions. It operates as part of Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham's AMMACHI Labs and the Center for Women’s Empowerment & Gender Equality (CWEGE), which are thematic research centers in Kerala, India. The fund supports projects in skill development, rural technologies, water and sanitation, and gender equality, often in collaboration with government and international organizations.
objectives: Strengthen the economic fiber and contribute to social stability of the nation by empowering India’s masses
Provide innovative technological solutions and resources for physical, vocational and social skill development
Address human sorrow and hardship with empathy, letting research and experience guide judgment and compassion guide decisions
Conduct research and design technologies to solve social problems leading to inclusive development of under-served communities
Promote women’s empowerment and gender equality through technology and innovation
Develop scalable and cost-effective implementation solutions to impact the livelihood of impoverished communities
Foster community participation and field engagement in rural and vulnerable areas
Support government initiatives such as Open Defecation Free (ODF) Villages and Swachh Bharat Campaign
eligibility: Eligibility varies by specific project; for PhD programs, candidates require a Master of Social Work (MSW) or related social science discipline, strong interest in gender justice, community resilience, and rural development, readiness for field-based research, and Kannada language proficiency is preferred. For skill development programs, eligibility includes women from socio-economically underserved communities, particularly in rural areas.
benefits: Benefits include vocational training in trades such as plumbing, carpentry, tailoring, beekeeping, seaweed cultivation, and two-wheeler repair; life skills and entrepreneurship training; access to microcredit loans and insurance; support for forming Self-Help Groups (SHGs); community-led sanitation initiatives; menstrual health and hygiene management through reusable pads; water quality monitoring training; and participation in government scheme awareness and access programs.
financial_support: Financial support includes start-up capital, marketing assistance, and access to microcredit loans from government-regulated banks and affordable insurance plans. The AmritaSREE program has provided $14.2 million in support for 2021 and 2022, and $1,200 each to widows of fishermen. Funding sources include United Nations Development Programme (UNDEP), Government of India, World Bank, and other international partners.
application_process: 1. Identify the specific program or initiative (e.g., PhD admissions, skill training, sanitation project). 2. Check eligibility criteria for the respective program. 3. Apply through the designated portal (e.g., Amrita SSBS PhD Admissions Process for research roles). 4. Submit required documents such as academic qualifications, statement of purpose, and language proficiency proof. 5. Await selection based on merit and alignment with program goals. 6. For community programs, engage through local outreach and field participation.
required_documents: Master of Social Work (MSW) or related social science degree certificate
Certificate of Incorporation or registration (for organizational applications)
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round for most programs.
implementing_agency: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham (University) through AMMACHI Labs and the Center for Women’s Empowerment & Gender Equality (CWEGE)
caveats: Program-specific eligibility criteria apply; not all benefits are available to all applicants
Field-based research and community engagement are mandatory for certain roles
Kannada language proficiency is preferred for Karnataka-based projects
Funding and support are subject to availability and project approval
Some initiatives require collaboration with government or partner institutions
